flags.observation: Thesis arrives only as an open question, "who paid when the banks crashed?"; no plain statement of the deck thesis follows in the intro.
Single onboarding beat: no speaker, no premise of what we are doing; the car setup has no clear punch a normie can catch.
Dog whistles limited to names from the next two cards; card-source insider details (birthday toast, General Counsel, Carroll Quigley) unused.
Punch hinges on "I lose my keys", a muddled consequence of a totaled car; the beat-1 question who paid stays implicit.
"gold for assets they do not possess" garbles the card: certificates represent assets the Fed lacks, not gold traded away for them.
Dropping "laugh at" leaves "Congressional funding" as a bare fragment that reads as if the Board receives it; card meaning lost.
Actor shifted: on the card the NY Fed exerts dominance; the line makes the Wall Street banks the subject.
Image words casino and table cut; "collapsed, public never leaves" no longer says what collapsed or what the public never leaves.
Card reports a claim, "They say the crashes they engineer"; the line drops the attribution and states engineered crashes as fact.
Simile truncated: "like vampires fight" ends without its object; two colons in a row make the beat stumble.
Card says "cuts parasites, not funding"; "cut funding parasites" blurs or inverts that claim, closing clause is a passive fragment.
"Int." is a printed abbreviation, not a sung word; the spoken form is left open.
"Four Hundred Twenty-Two" drops the dollar of the card name "$422"; amount not written out as sung.
115 characters with opener and a long spelled number; not sayable in one breath. Beats 4, 23, 24 also exceed 110.
"Global." opener only repeats the card name; no therefore or but link from the Feudal Endgame.
"Choice." repeats the last word of its own line; same label pattern at beat 30 and beat 19: labels, not bridges.
"Street account." is an opaque opener, neither bridge nor callback, and pre-echoes "accounting" in the same line.
The card is a first-person tantrum, "Lose? Please."; the line flattens it to third person and the character voice is gone.
The person behind the card vanishes; "mutual credit, graphic design and arrogance" reads as a noun list with no want or grudge.
